headline.headline: PHILLIES ERASE TWO-RUN DEFICIT WITH SIX-RUN SEVENTH TO DOWN NATIONALS, 6-3
headline.deck: Philadelphia bats explode in seventh inning, silencing Washington after early lead
headline.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The Washington Nationals held a 2-0 lead through six innings at Citizens Bank Park on Monday night, looking every bit like a team capable of stealing a road victory. Then the seventh inning arrived, and the Philadelphia Phillies sent six runs across the plate in a single frame to turn a deficit into a rout, winning 6-3 before 41,115 fans.

The Nationals had built their advantage with a run in the first inning and another in the second, but their bats went completely silent from the third inning through the ninth, held scoreless over the final seven frames. Philadelphia's offense, dormant for much of the night, detonated in the seventh to seize control and never looked back, adding two more runs in the eighth to close out Washington for good.

The loss was compounded by a pair of hit batsmen issued against Bryan De La Cruz, who was struck twice by Philadelphia pitching, while Washington's Yean plunked a Phillies batter as well. The game was completed in 2 hours and 38 minutes, and the Phillies head into Tuesday having demonstrated they can manufacture a big inning even when trailing deep into a ballgame.

secondary.headline: CUBS JUMP ON DODGERS EARLY, ROLL TO 10-5 WIN AT WRIGLEY
secondary.deck: Chicago builds lead through six innings as Los Angeles never finds its footing
secondary.body:
CHICAGO — The Chicago Cubs outlasted the Los Angeles Dodgers 10-5 at Wrigley Field on Monday, using a steady accumulation of runs across the middle innings to pull away from one of the National League's marquee clubs. Tommy Edman connected for his third home run of the season as part of the Cubs' offensive effort, which produced runs in five of nine innings and drew 39,384 fans to the North Side.

Los Angeles struck first with three runs in the top of the first, giving the Dodgers an early 3-2 edge, but Chicago answered with two runs of its own in the opening frame and never fell behind again. The Cubs pushed ahead with two more in the second, two in the third, and three in the sixth inning to put the game out of reach. The Dodgers managed only single-run innings in the fourth and sixth and could not mount a serious threat in the final three frames.

secondary.headline: PIRATES HOLD OFF BREWERS, 4-3, AS SPROAT EARNS WIN ON ROAD
secondary.deck: Pittsburgh survives Milwaukee late-game push to claim narrow victory in Wisconsin
secondary.body:
MILWAUKEE — The Pittsburgh Pirates scored three runs in the third inning and one more in the fourth, then held on through a nervous finish as the Milwaukee Brewers cut the deficit to one run and threatened through the final frames, falling 4-3 at American Family Field on Monday before a crowd of 30,684. Pitcher Sproat earned his third win of the season in the decision.

Milwaukee chipped away with a run in the fifth and two more in the sixth to close within one, but Pittsburgh's bullpen held the Brewers scoreless over the final three innings to preserve the victory. An HBP on Mitchell, struck by Brewers pitcher Soto, added to the night's tension. The Pirates, who have now won a game decided by a single run, will look to build on the road result as the second half of the season progresses.

secondary.headline: WEMBANYAMA GATHERS SPURS IN FRANCE AS SAN ANTONIO PLOTS PLAYOFF PUSH
secondary.deck: Victor Wembanyama hosts eight to ten teammates for summer workouts abroad
secondary.body:
PARIS — Victor Wembanyama is bringing the San Antonio Spurs together on his home turf. The franchise cornerstone is hosting eight to ten teammates in France this week for organized workouts, a voluntary gathering that underscores the young star's growing leadership role within a Spurs organization that continues to build around his generational talent.

The workouts represent an early sign of cohesion for a San Antonio roster that will be counting on Wembanyama to carry a heavier burden as the team's ambitions grow heading into the 2026-27 season. While the NBA and NHL playoffs are still in their second rounds and the summer calendar is only beginning, moves like this one signal that the Spurs are not waiting for training camp to start the work of improvement.

column.headline: THOSE PHILLIES COULDN'T BUY A RUN FOR SIX INNINGS, THEN THEY BOUGHT THE WHOLE STORE
column.body:
There is a particular kind of torture that Citizens Bank Park regulars know well. It is the torture of watching a Philadelphia offense go quiet for inning after inning while the opposing pitcher strands runners and the scoreboard stays frozen. Monday night against Washington delivered exactly that sensation for six full innings, the Nationals nursing a two-run lead they had no business protecting as long as they did.

Then the seventh inning came, and six runs went up in a blink, and every person who stayed in their seat through that slow burn was rewarded. That is the ruthless arithmetic of baseball. A team can be utterly silent for eighteen outs and then rearrange the entire game in one chaotic frame. The Phillies did not need a comeback narrative or a hero's speech. They just needed one good inning, and they got it at exactly the right moment.

story.headline: BURLESON BLASTS THREE TWO-RUN HOMERS AS CARDINALS STUN YANKEES, 13-7
story.deck: St. Louis erupts for seven in the eighth to bury New York at home
story.body:
ST. LOUIS -- Alec Burleson crushed three two-run home runs Monday, capping his demolition with a drive into the second deck in right field as the St. Louis Cardinals unleashed a seven-run eighth inning to outlast the New York Yankees 13-7 at Yankee Stadium. Burleson's big night headlined a Cardinals offensive barrage that also featured home runs from Nolan Gorman, Tyler O'Neill, Thairo Estrada, and others, with St. Louis sending 13 runners to the plate in the decisive eighth frame alone to turn a close contest into a rout before 38,151 fans.

The Yankees had pulled within striking distance entering the late innings, plating four runs in the seventh to make it a game, but the Cardinals bullpen and bats proved too much. New York received home run contributions from Jahmai Jones and Michael Caballero, and Aaron Judge connected for his 24th of the season, yet the Yankees stranded nine baserunners and could not contain St. Louis once the Cardinals offense ignited. The game consumed three hours and 25 minutes, the longest of Monday's slate.

Elsewhere around the majors, Bryce Harper launched his 24th home run and Philadelphia rallied for six unanswered runs over the final three innings to defeat Washington 6-3, overcoming a 2-0 deficit through six. In Chicago, Seiya Suzuki belted his 19th homer and the Cubs pounded out a 10-5 victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers at Wrigley Field. Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero crushed his 32nd home run of the season as the Rays held off Colorado 13-9 in a slugfest at Coors Field.

story.headline: KNICKS SHAKE UP FRONT OFFICE AS ROSAS PARTS WAYS WITH NEW YORK AFTER FOUR SEASONS
story.deck: Senior vice president of basketball operations Gersson Rosas exits organization amid roster rebuild
story.body:
The New York Knicks are parting ways with senior vice president of basketball operations Gersson Rosas after four seasons, league sources confirmed Tuesday, triggering another round of front office turbulence for a franchise that has long struggled to establish stable leadership. Rosas, who previously served as general manager of the Minnesota Timberwolves before joining Madison Square Garden, leaves the organization as the Knicks attempt to position themselves as legitimate Eastern Conference contenders heading into the 2026-27 season.

The departure raises immediate questions about the team's roster construction philosophy and its relationships with key players, including All-Star Julius Randle and rising guard Jalen Brunson, both of whom have been cornerstones of the franchise's recent revival. Sources close to the organization indicated that differing visions over personnel decisions and the direction of the rebuild contributed to the split, though the Knicks declined to comment publicly on the circumstances surrounding Rosas's exit.

The timing compounds an already eventful offseason for New York, which has been active in free agency and trade discussions throughout July. Meanwhile, across the league, San Antonio Spurs phenom Victor Wembanyama is drawing attention of a different kind, as retired Heat superstar Chris Bosh publicly cautioned the 22-year-old about blood clot risks following Wembanyama's own health scare, urging the French star to remain vigilant with his prescribed treatment regimen.

story.headline: SHARKS LOCK UP GRAF, PENGUINS EXTEND NOVAK AS NHL OFFSEASON HEATS UP
story.deck: San Jose and Pittsburgh make moves while Sweden's Färjestad rescinds Cal Foote's contract amid fan backlash.
story.body:
The San Jose Sharks wasted no time securing one of their brightest young forwards, agreeing to a three-year contract worth $12.75 million with Collin Graf on Tuesday. Graf, 24, emerged as a dependable two-way presence for San Jose last season, posting 21 goals and 25 assists across 81 games. The deal averages $4.25 million per year and signals the rebuilding Sharks' commitment to building around homegrown talent rather than chasing big-name free agents.

In Pittsburgh, the Penguins locked up veteran forward Tommy Novak on a three-year extension Friday, adding stability to a roster in transition. Novak, known for his reliable defensive zone play and faceoff ability, gives Pittsburgh a dependable middle-six option as the franchise works to reshape its identity in the post-Sidney Crosby era. Meanwhile, the IIHF confirmed Russia will remain barred from four major tournaments in 2027, continuing the federation's policy of exclusion following the ongoing geopolitical crisis that prompted the original ban.

On the European front, Swedish Elite League club Färjestad BK rescinded defenseman Cal Foote's contract Thursday following a fierce backlash from supporters, an embarrassing reversal that drew sharp attention across the hockey world. Foote, the son of former NHL blueliner Adam Foote, had appeared set to play in Sweden before fan pressure forced the club's hand. Elsewhere, top prospect Gavin McKenna headlined an NHL rookie roundtable Tuesday, charming reporters with candid answers about his game and a self-deprecating most-embarrassing-moment story that quickly circulated across hockey social media.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL TEAMS RESHAPE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are betting big on new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has erupted into one of the most aggressive quarterback markets in recent memory, with multiple franchises overhauling their most important positions just months after Super Bowl LX wrapped up in February. The Cleveland Browns made the splashiest move of the spring, trading three draft picks to acquire veteran quarterback Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings, reuniting Darnold with offensive coordinator Ken Dorsey in what Cleveland brass is calling a true franchise reset. The Las Vegas Raiders, meanwhile, signed free agent Gardner Minshew to a two-year, $48 million deal, signaling a complete departure from their rebuilding philosophy under first-year head coach Mike Vrabel.

The 2026 NFL Draft, held last month in Indianapolis, continued to reshape the league's competitive landscape. The Tennessee Titans selected Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders with the second overall pick after trading down from the top spot in a deal with the New York Giants, who grabbed pass rusher James Pearce Jr. out of Tennessee. Draft analysts praised the Giants for the value of that haul, noting that new general manager Terry Fontenot made the bold call just 72 hours after taking the job. Sanders arrived in Nashville to immediate fanfare, drawing comparisons to his father Deion's swagger but also facing pointed questions about his ability to handle an NFL pass rush.

On the trade front, wide receiver DK Metcalf officially cleared waivers after the Seattle Seahawks released him in a cost-cutting move, and within 48 hours he agreed to terms with the Dallas Cowboys on a restructured deal worth up to $31 million annually. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones called it the most exciting receiver acquisition in the franchise's history, a characterization that drew skepticism from analysts pointing to Michael Irvin's legacy. Training camps open in late July, and the combination of new quarterbacks, blockbuster trades, and a draft class loaded at the edges means the 2026 season promises to look dramatically different from the one that just concluded.
